transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess… I’m here because I’ve been feeling like I don’t really deserve the trust people put in me. I keep going over small things at work, little clinical imperfections, and it feels like they prove I’m… a dangerous doctor.
Do you find yourself having repetitive thoughts that you can't seem to get out of your head?
Yes… mostly about work. I keep replaying small things I did, like little imperfections, and it turns into this thought that I shouldn’t be trusted… that I might be a dangerous doctor.
Do you feel like you have to do certain things over and over to reduce your anxiety about being a dangerous doctor?
I… don’t know. I wouldn’t say I have a specific thing I do over and over, not really. It’s more that the thoughts just sit there.
Do you feel like you have to behave in certain ways to reduce your anxiety?
Not really… I mean, I might try to be extra careful, but I don’t think there’s a set behavior I have to do to make the anxiety go away. It’s more just… in my head.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to repeat certain actions or mental acts in response to your thoughts about being a dangerous doctor?
No… I don’t think so. I don’t feel driven to repeat something like that. It’s more just the thoughts being there, and I get stuck with them.
Have these thoughts and feelings about being a dangerous doctor interfered with your daily life or relationships?

Yeah… somewhat. I’m still going to clinic, but I’ve had to ask for help with some non-urgent admin stuff. And I’ve been avoiding seeing people outside work. I just don’t really trust my judgment or my energy lately, so… it’s starting to affect things.
Do you feel like there's something specific you need to think about or do when these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor come up, to make them go away or feel better?
I don’t think there’s a specific thing. I might sort of… go over it in my head, but it doesn’t really make it go away. I’m not doing some particular routine or anything.
Do you feel like you must think certain thoughts to prevent something bad from happening when you have these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor?
No… I don’t think so. It’s not like I have to think something specific to stop something happening. The thoughts just… sit there.
Do you feel anxious when interacting with others, outside of the thoughts about being a dangerous doctor?
Not really… I mean, I can be a bit tense around people lately, but I wouldn’t say it’s separate from all that. I haven’t really noticed a different kind of anxiety, if that’s what you mean.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are a part of yourself, or do they feel like they're coming from outside of yourself?

It feels like it’s me thinking it… not like a voice from outside or anything. But I can’t really shake it. Even if I check the chart and there’s nothing there, I still believe I must have harmed someone somehow… with a delay or a message that wasn’t right. Eventually people will find it.
Do you ever feel the need to check things repeatedly to make sure everything is okay?
I don’t know… not repeatedly, exactly. I might look over something to be sure, but I wouldn’t say I’m stuck checking it over and over.
Do you have thoughts that keep repeating in your mind even when you try to stop thinking about them?
Yeah… I guess so. It’s mostly the same kind of thing looping — that I don’t really deserve people trusting me, and I keep going back over small clinical things like they prove I’m dangerous somehow.
Do you think these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are reasonable or do they seem irrational to you?

I know it probably sounds irrational when I say it out loud. But it doesn’t feel that way to me. Even when I check the chart and there’s nothing showing anything bad happened, I still can’t shake the belief that some small delay or imperfect message from me hurt someone, and that eventually people will find out.
Do you feel like you have to think about these imperfections at work for a certain amount of time to feel better?
Not really a set amount of time, no. It’s more like… it just sits there, and I go over it, but I don’t have a rule about it making me feel better.
Do you feel like you have to think about these thoughts to prevent something bad from happening?

I don’t know if it’s to prevent something, exactly. It feels more like… if I don’t keep going over it, I’m missing the thing that proves I hurt someone. Even when the chart looks fine, I still think some delay or message I sent could’ve quietly harmed a patient, and eventually everyone will see it.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are in line with your own beliefs and values?

Not really. I mean… I don’t want to be that kind of doctor. I care about doing right by people.

But I keep feeling like I don’t deserve the trust they put in me, and every small mistake or imperfect thing I did feels like proof that I’m dangerous somehow.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are unwanted and pop into your mind without you trying to think about them?

Yeah… I guess they are unwanted. I’m not trying to think about it.

It’s more like I’ll be at work and then I start replaying some small clinical thing I didn’t do perfectly, and it turns into… maybe that proves I shouldn’t be trusted, or that I’m dangerous somehow. I don’t want to think that.
Do you feel like you have to mentally or physically do something to try to make these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor go away or to prevent the bad things you worry about from happening?

I’m not sure. I don’t think I have a specific thing I do, like a ritual or anything.

Sometimes I check or replay things in my head, but I don’t know if it’s to make the thoughts go away exactly. It just… happens.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor force themselves into your mind without you wanting them to?

Yes… I think so. I don’t want them there.

I’ll just be trying to get through work, and then I’m back on some small thing I didn’t do perfectly, and it feels like it means I don’t deserve people trusting me… like it proves I’m dangerous. It’s hard to stop once it starts.
Do you feel like these thoughts about being a dangerous doctor are something you're forcing yourself to think about, or do they just appear in your mind on their own?

They just sort of appear on their own.

I’m not trying to sit there and think about it. I’ll notice some small thing I maybe didn’t do perfectly, and then it turns into… me feeling like I don’t deserve people trusting me. Like it means I’m dangerous somehow.
